title: Sections over the point commute with scalar extension
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\Ql$ in $\Qlb$ write $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ for the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], for $F=E,L$. For $K\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] put $T_{L/E}K=K\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, meaning the strict-tower integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], which belongs to $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_L)$ by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. Let $\Gamma(s,-)$ be sections over the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, applied termwise and passed to derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. There are isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_L)$, natural in $K$,
$$
 \varphi_{L/E,K}:\Gamma(s,T_{L/E}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L.
$$
Here tensor on module complexes is termwise ordinary tensor. The isomorphism is the inverse of the composite of the canonical sections-tensor map with sections of the canonical completion comparison $\chi_{L/E,K}:K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}K$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]; explicitly, if $\theta_{L/E,K}:\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\to\Gamma(s,K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)$ is induced by tensoring sections, then $\varphi_{L/E,K}=(\Gamma(s,\chi_{L/E,K})\circ\theta_{L/E,K})^{-1}$.

For $L=E$ this is the identity under the multiplication and completeness identifications $T_{E/E}K\cong K$. For $E\subset L\subset M$, let $a^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,L,E,K}:T_{M/L}T_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{M/E}K$ be the integral associator obtained by conjugating the ordinary derived-tensor associator $(K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)\otimes^L_{R_L}R_M\cong K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_M$ by the canonical comparisons $\chi$. Write $a^{\mathrm{mod}}$ for the module-complex associator $(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_M\cong N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_M$. Then
$$
 \varphi_{M/E,K}\circ\Gamma(s,a^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,L,E,K})
 =a^{\mathrm{mod}}\circ(\varphi_{L/E,K}\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_M)\circ\varphi_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}.
$$
Tensoring with $L$ over $\mathcal O_L$ gives natural isomorphisms
$$
 \Gamma(s,T_{L/E}K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L\cong
 (\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E)\otimes_E L
$$
in $D(L)$, with the same identity and composition compatibilities.

proof.text: For each coefficient field $F$ under consideration, apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] to $X=s$. Its noetherian hypothesis holds: the spectrum of a field has only one point and its coordinate ring is noetherian. Its continuous-function sheaf description identifies $R_F$ canonically with $V\mapsto C(|V|,\mathcal O_F)$, compatibly with the finite quotient projections. In particular $\Gamma(s,R_F)=C(\{*\},\mathcal O_F)=\mathcal O_F$, by evaluation at the unique point. These identifications respect coefficient inclusions, since their maps to each quotient send a constant value to its residue and the inverse-limit projections determine a map uniquely. Apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] to $Y=s$: $R_L$ is a finite free $R_E$-module sheaf, of rank $d=[L:E]$. Choose a sheaf-module basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$, meaning an isomorphism $R_E^{\oplus d}\to R_L$. Taking sections identifies it with an isomorphism $\mathcal O_E^{\oplus d}\to\mathcal O_L$: finite direct sums of sheaves of modules are finite products, and products of sheaves are sectionwise. Thus these same global sections $b_i$ are an $\mathcal O_E$-basis of $\mathcal O_L$. This derives precisely the compatible basis needed below; it does not identify the completed coefficient sheaf with the discrete constant sheaf.

proof.text: For any sheaf $F$ of $R_E$-modules define the balanced map $\theta_F:\Gamma(s,F)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\to\Gamma(s,F\otimes_{R_E}R_L)$ by $n\otimes a\mapsto n\otimes a$, where the tensor on the right is the image of the sectionwise tensor in the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Under the basis of step 1, $F\otimes_{R_E}R_L\cong F^{\oplus d}$: the inverse coordinate maps send $f\otimes\sum_i r_i b_i$ to $(r_i f)_i$. Taking sections gives $\Gamma(s,F)^{\oplus d}$, while the source of $\theta_F$ has the same description, and $\theta_F$ is the identity on each coordinate. Its inverse sends $(n_i)_i$ to $\sum_i n_i\otimes b_i$. In particular it is an isomorphism. For $a,c\in\mathcal O_L$, the equality $\theta_F(n\otimes ac)=c\theta_F(n\otimes a)$ shows $\mathcal O_L$-linearity. Every sheaf map commutes with this formula, so it is natural. Apply degreewise to any complex; differentials commute with $\theta$ by the same formula. The basis proves both tensor functors exact, since they are finite direct sums, so they preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Exactness of $\Gamma(s,-)$ from [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] supplies quasi-isomorphism preservation on sections. These are inverse chain maps, not an assertion that arbitrary sheaf tensor products are computed sectionwise.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1); explicit finite-basis sections-tensor calculation written by the worker

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Then $P\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ computes $K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The degreewise map of step 2, applied to $P$, therefore gives $\theta_{L/E,K}$ on derived categories: $\Gamma(s,P)\to\Gamma(s,K)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], and its tensor with $\mathcal O_L$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 1's basis. The integral input $K$ is derived complete by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Hence [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives the specified natural isomorphism $\chi_{L/E,K}$, and $\Gamma(s,\chi_{L/E,K})$ is an isomorphism. Define $\varphi$ as the inverse of their composite, as in the statement. Naturality for chain maps follows from step 2 and naturality of $\chi$. For an arbitrary derived morphism use a roof $K\xleftarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{f}J$ with $q$ a quasi-isomorphism. The termwise functors $A(C)=\Gamma(s,C)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ and $B(C)=\Gamma(s,C\otimes_{R_E}R_L)$ both preserve every quasi-isomorphism by step 2, not only those between K-flat complexes. For a chain map $g:C\to C'$ the formula on tensors gives $B(g)\theta_C=\theta_{C'}A(g)$. Applying this to $q,f$ and inverting $A(q),B(q)$ gives $B(f)B(q)^{-1}\theta_K=\theta_J A(f)A(q)^{-1}$, the required roof naturality. For a K-flat resolution $P\to C$, step 2 also makes $P\otimes_{R_E}R_L\to C\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ a quasi-isomorphism, so [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies this termwise functor canonically with derived change of rings. Thus the roof calculation proves naturality and independence of representatives for the specified $\theta_{L/E,K}$; composing with the natural $\chi$ proves the assertion for $\varphi$.

proof.text: For $E\subset L\subset M$ put $R=R_E$, $S=R_L$, $U=R_M$. The complex $P\otimes_R S$ is K-flat over $S$ with flat terms by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], so all ordinary derived tensors below are computed by the same complexes. The inverse balanced chain maps $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto p\otimes ab$ and $p\otimes b\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes b$ give $(P\otimes_R S)\otimes_S U\cong P\otimes_R U$; the balancing equation $(p\otimes a)\otimes b=(p\otimes1)\otimes ab$ verifies the inverse. For a chain map $g:P\to Q$, either order of applying $g$ and the associator sends $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $g(p)\otimes ab$. For a roof $P\xleftarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{f}Q$, the resulting commutative squares for $q$ and $f$, with the arrows induced by $q$ inverted, give the naturality square for $f q^{-1}$, as in step 3. All tensor functors here preserve quasi-isomorphisms by the finite-free bases from step 1, so those inverses exist. Since $T_{L/E}K$ is constructible and derived complete by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] and [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] also applies to the input $T_{L/E}K$ for $L\subset M$. Define the integral associator to be the following composite: $T_{M/L}T_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\chi_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}^{-1}}T_{L/E}K\otimes^L_S U\xrightarrow{\chi_{L/E,K}^{-1}\otimes1}(K\otimes^L_R S)\otimes^L_S U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{assoc}}K\otimes^L_R U\xrightarrow{\chi_{M/E,K}}T_{M/E}K$. Every arrow is an isomorphism and natural; the formula fixes the actual integral associator rather than taking it from a rational-only associativity theorem. The ordinary unit is $p\otimes r\mapsto rp$. For an identity extension the comparison $\chi$ is the completeness unit by the finite-free comparison node, so the identity identification is $T_{E/E}K\xrightarrow{\chi_{E/E,K}^{-1}}K\otimes^L_R R\xrightarrow{\mathrm{mult}}K$.

proof.text:
Before completion, the two sections-tensor comparisons for $E\subset L\subset M$ satisfy
$$
\Gamma(\alpha)\,\theta_{M/L,A}(\theta_{L/E,K}\otimes1)=\theta_{M/E,K}\,a^{\mathrm{mod}},\qquad A=K\otimes^L_R S,
$$
where $\alpha:A\otimes^L_S U\to K\otimes^L_R U$ is the ordinary associator from step 4. On complexes both sides send $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to the section $n\otimes ab$. Pure tensors generate the source in each degree, so the maps agree, including their coefficient actions; step 3 descends this equality to derived categories. To check every intervening completion map, abbreviate $C=\chi_{L/E,K}$, $D=\chi_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}$, $H=\chi_{M/E,K}$, and $F(B)=B\otimes^L_S U$. Thus step 4 defines $a^{\mathrm{int}}=H\alpha F(C^{-1})D^{-1}$. Naturality of $\theta$ from step 3, applied to the derived isomorphism $C:A\to T_{L/E}K$, says
$$
\theta_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}(\Gamma(C)\otimes1)=\Gamma(F(C))\theta_{M/L,A}.
$$
Writing $\psi_{L/E,K}=\Gamma(\chi_{L/E,K})\theta_{L/E,K}$, substitution now gives the explicit cancellations
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma(a^{\mathrm{int}})\,\psi_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}(\psi_{L/E,K}\otimes1)
&=\Gamma(H)\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(F(C^{-1}))\Gamma(D^{-1})\Gamma(D)\,
\theta_{M/L,T_{L/E}K}(\Gamma(C)\otimes1)(\theta_{L/E,K}\otimes1)\\
&=\Gamma(H)\Gamma(\alpha)\Gamma(F(C^{-1}))\Gamma(F(C))\,
\theta_{M/L,A}(\theta_{L/E,K}\otimes1)\\
&=\Gamma(H)\Gamma(\alpha)\theta_{M/L,A}(\theta_{L/E,K}\otimes1)\\
&=\psi_{M/E,K}\,a^{\mathrm{mod}}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The common domain is $(\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_M$. Multiplying by the inverse maps $\varphi=\psi^{-1}$ gives the statement's composition equation. For $L=E$, $\theta(n\otimes r)$ followed by multiplication is $rn$, so under the completeness-unit identification of step 4 the comparison is the identity. For four coefficient fields, each ordinary iterated associator sends $(((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c)$ to $n\otimes abc$; substitution of the displayed conjugation cancels each intermediate $\chi^{-1}\chi$, proving the iterated coherence. The comparisons $C,D,H$ are natural isomorphisms by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].

source.place: Stagewise finite-extension passage: explicit pure-tensor computation of identity and composition coherence

proof.text: Put $N=\Gamma(s,K)$. Tensoring the integral comparison with $L$ gives $\Gamma(s,T_{L/E}K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L\cong(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L\cong N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}L$, where the second map sends $(n\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $n\otimes ab$ and its inverse sends $n\otimes b$ to $(n\otimes1)\otimes b$. The DVR assertion [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $E$ the fraction field of $\mathcal O_E$. For a nonzero $r\in\mathcal O_E$, multiplication by $r$ on $N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}L$ is invertible, its inverse multiplying the $L$-coordinate by $r^{-1}$. Thus there are inverse maps $(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E)\otimes_E L\leftrightarrows N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}L$ given by $(n\otimes x)\otimes b\mapsto n\otimes xb$ and $n\otimes b\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes b$; moving a denominator across the tensor relation proves the other composite is the identity. These maps commute with differentials. Localization is exact: a fraction maps to zero precisely when some nonzero denominator annihilates its numerator, so localizing preserves kernels as well as images; hence all termwise localizations preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Extension from $E$ to $L$ is exact because every finite-dimensional field extension has a basis (successively choose a vector outside the span until the finite dimension is exhausted), so its underlying functor is a finite direct sum. The same reasoning applies to $L\subset M$. Consequently these are isomorphisms in $D(L)$, natural in $K$. On a tower all localization and associativity maps send a pure tensor with coefficient factors $a,b,c$ to their product $abc$; applying step 5's integral equation and these balanced maps proves the rational identity and composition equations, including fractions since the inverted coefficients act by invertible maps.
